text: Writing clean code is essential for any developer, whether you work alone or in a team. The main goal is to make your code as readable as possible, so that anyone can understand it quickly. This starts with using clear naming conventions; for example, a variable called `userAge` is far better than `x`. Instead of writing long, complex blocks, you should break your logic into small, focused functions that each do one specific job. This makes your code easier to test and debug. Ultimately, clean code improves maintainability, meaning you and others can easily update it in the future without creating new problems. It saves time and reduces frustration.
